title: HCP — Set Directive — payload
description: The request payload of the HCP 2.0-draft-3 Set directive operation (HCP 6.4, 5.4; `POST /v2/directives` in HCP 9.2, 9.4.15): a Management Client, acting for the Context Subject or a delegate, sets a directive telling clients what they may do with context they receive, or on the person's behalf. HCP defines no request schema for this operation; the members come from HCP 9.4.15 and the directive of HCP 6.4. The provider sets `directiveId`, `setBy` and `createdAt`; none is taken from the request. The outer document members (id, type, issuer, recipient, issuedAt, expiresAt, proof) are owned by the framework — SPEC §6.3. Every maxLength, maxItems and maxProperties in this schema is a Trust Tasks framework bound (SPEC §7.3 item 19), not an HCP requirement; so is every minLength or minItems of 1 on a member HCP's own schema allows to be empty.

action.description: HCP `action` (HCP 6.4, 9.4.15): what the directive governs: `share` (passing received context to another agent, HCP 3.12), `sign` (signing, agreeing to or committing to anything on the Context Subject's behalf), `transact` (spending, buying or entering a contract on their behalf), or an absolute URI naming another action (HCP A.3).

effect.description: HCP `effect` (HCP 6.4, 9.4.15): `deny`, the client MUST NOT take the action; `ask-first`, the client MUST obtain the Context Subject's confirmation each time before taking it; `permit`, the client may take it without asking. HCP's own values, carried verbatim.

text.description: HCP `text` (HCP 6.4, 9.4.15): the directive in the Context Subject's words, shown to them when it is set and delivered to every client it applies to. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

categories.description: HCP `categories` (HCP 6.4, 9.4.15): the categories whose context the directive governs. Absent means every category, held now or later. A delegate's directive must stay within the delegation's scope (HCP 6.4, 17.4). The maxItems is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

operators.description: HCP `operators` (HCP 6.4, 9.4.15): the Client Operators the directive applies to, each a DNS domain or an operator identifier, matched as for standing rules (HCP 6.3). Absent means every operator. The maxItems is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement.

accessToken.description: The Management Client's HCP access token (HCP 9.3), carried unchanged. HCP's HTTP Binding sends it as a Bearer token; this member carries it in the document. The provider validates it exactly as over HTTP and treats it as opaque. The maxLength is a framework bound, not an HCP requirement. OPTIONAL: where it is absent, the provider authenticates the request's `issuer` VID, by the REQUIRED request proof, as a Management Client the Authorizing Principal enrolled (HCP 3.2.3), and refuses any other issuer with permissionDenied; where it is present, the token rules apply unchanged. Pending HCP confirmation (question 56).

Response.title: HCP — Set Directive — response payload
Response.description: The directive is set. Carries HCP's `201` result, the directive with its `directiveId` and `createdAt` (HCP 9.4.15), wrapped in `directive`. Failures use trust-task-error, not this shape.

directive.description: The directive as the provider holds it (HCP 6.4, 9.4.15): the requested `action`, `effect`, `text`, `categories` and `operators`, with `directiveId`, `setBy` and `createdAt` set by the provider.
